answer: A storage market can require a separately sealed dataset replica for every rewarded identity. The encoding mixes an identity key with unpredictable randomness; audits request proofs from random chunks, so the same bytes cannot satisfy two names. Calling copies ripple or yarrow does not help: each needs its own disk space and ongoing audit work. This turns cheap identity multiplication into a physical resource expense, not a fable of perfect uniqueness. Security depends on a sound proof-of-replication scheme.
